## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Moha Sutta* ("Delusion", Iti 3) is the third discourse in the first division of the *Itivuttaka* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. The core teaching of the sutta proclaims that abandoning delusion (*moha*) guarantees the attainment of non-return (*anāgāmitā*).

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus shows that the text shares extensive stock formulas across the *Itivuttaka*, displaying near-verbatim structural parallels with neighboring suttas dealing with defilements, including the *Lobha Sutta* (Iti 1), the *Dosa Sutta* (Iti 2), the *Kodha Sutta* (Iti 4), the *Makkha Sutta* (Iti 5), and the *Māna Sutta* (Iti 6), as well as sharing passages with the *Itivuttaka-aṭṭhakathā* and later sub-commentaries such as the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments are also identified by DharmaNexus with the Chinese *Dīrgha-āgama* (T 1) [DharmaNexus].
